scope: 2D frames from DICOM raster image objects, including CT, MR, CR, DX, intraoral, ultrasound and secondary capture; no volume rendering
display: Recorded effective source-frame/window/rescale/polarity or color transform, no inferred rotation or reflection. Unsupported pixel transformations/codecs produce explicit diagnostics.
preservation: Every supplied regular file is embedded unchanged, including empty, corrupt and unsupported files; rendering rejection is separate from source preservation
referenceCoverage: Only explicit Referenced SOP Instance UID occurrences in readable DICOM metadata establish known references. A clean reference report does not prove clinical study completeness. Duplicate target IDs are ambiguous; missing target files, invalid frames and class mismatches remain unresolved. An unassessed diagnostic reference row at /REFERENCE_SCAN_INCOMPLETE with null UID records a scan failure after successful metadata parsing; it is not an invented DICOM reference. Unreadable originals are reported as unknown coverage separately.
sourceRoleSemantics: Caller supplied label, not an automatic deidentification claim. Create separate packages and output directories for archival masters and approved deidentified derivatives; original bytes are never edited.
integrity: SHA-256 detects disagreement with the manifest; without signing it does not establish authenticity. Verify PDF/A, stored-source hashes, external-source byte matches, metadata accuracy and unresolved references as distinct results.
deferred: non-raster DICOM presentation including video, waveforms and structured reports
imageClasses: Pixel-bearing DICOM Image Storage classes; non-image objects remain embedded with diagnostics
frames: PDF references use source frame 1. The viewer can select individual frames. Multi-frame objects are not treated as volumes.
codecLimitations: PDF references require bundled pure-Java codecs. JPEG-LS and JPEG2000 originals can be explored using permissively licensed local browser codecs even when the PDF contains a diagnostic page. This does not claim a PDF preview exists.
